title: Genesis 28 — Yitzchaq's commission, Esav's third wife, and Ya'aqov's ladder at Beit-El

verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed MT: *va-yiqra Yitzchaq el-Ya'aqov va-yvarekh oto va-y'tzavehu va-yomer lo lo-tiqach ishah mi-b'not Kena'an*. ASV-baseline translation; lexemes match source; no editorial choices to verify.
Re-parsed MT. *Padenah Aram* preserved in transliteration; *beit Betu'el* preserved as house construct. Faithful ASV-baseline rendering.

Re-parsed MT: *v-El Shaddai yvarekh otkha v-yafrekha v-yarbekha v-hayita li-q'hal amim*. The *q'hal amim* construct is grammatically explicit; cross-corpus distribution to Gen 35:11 (q'hal goyim) and Gen 48:4 verified in lexical search. NRSV-adjacent 'assembly of peoples' preserves the cultic-register against ASV/KJV 'company.' Defensible.

Re-parsed MT: *v-yiten l'kha et-birkat Avraham*. The lexicalization of 'blessing of Avraham' as a discrete transferable item is HB-internal-explicit at this verse; cross-corpus Pauline reception (Gal 3:14) flagged-not-preempted in entry. ASV-baseline 'the blessing of Avraham' is faithful.
Re-parsed MT. Narrative verse; faithful rendering with names preserved in transliteration per chapter convention.

Re-parsed MT. The Editor's call not to extend *morat-ruach-bitterness-of-spirit-esau-hittite-wives* appliesTo to 28:6 is correct: the lexeme *morat ruach* is absent here; thematic-without-lexical link does not warrant extension under current convention.
Re-parsed MT: *va-yishma Ya'aqov el-aviv v-el-imo va-yelekh padenah Aram*. Faithful narrative rendering.
Re-parsed MT: *va-yar Esav ki ra'ot b'not Kena'an b-einei Yitzchaq aviv*. Faithful rendering.
Re-parsed MT. The added wife from the Yishma'elite line; *al-nashav* rendered 'in addition to' (correct ANE polygamous register).
Re-parsed MT. The travel-itinerary opening of the Bethel pericope. Transliteration preserved.

Re-parsed MT. *Va-yifga ba-maqom* — verb *paga* (H6293) is genuinely polysemic; ASV-baseline 'lighted upon' preserves the chance-encounter register that the v 16 *anokhi lo yadati* discovery-formula assumes. The definite-articled *ha-maqom* technical-cultic-site reading (Sarna p. 198; Speiser p. 218) is documented in commentary. Defensible.

citations: Houtman, 'What did Jacob see in his dream at Bethel?' VT 27 (1977) pp. 337-351
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed MT: *va-yachalom v-hineh sulam mutzav artzah v-rosho magia ha-shamayma v-hineh mal'akhei Elohim olim v-yordim bo*. The *sulam* hapax-status, the etymological derivation from *s-l-l*, and the Akkadian *simmiltu ša šamê* parallel are all documentary. The 'stairway' rendering is the mainstream modern-critical preference (Houtman 1977 is the foundational treatment); the ASV-departure is editorially-motivated by the chapter's Akkadian-ziggurat intertext (v 12 *rosho magia ha-shamayma* echoes Gen 11:4 *u-rosho ba-shamayim*; v 17 *sha'ar ha-shamayim* = *bab-ili*). The 'ladder' tradition is preserved in apparatus. The plural *malakhei Elohim olim v-yordim* with ascending-before-descending is grammatically explicit and patriarchal-corpus-unique; NT John 1:51 reception flagged-not-preempted. The two-entry coverage (plural-specific + singular-family) is defensible though I note the singular *malakh-elohim-messenger* appliesTo extension is a minor convention question — see glossaryReview.

citations: Alter The Five Books of Moses (2004) p. 149
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed MT: *v-hineh YHWH nitzav alav va-yomar ani YHWH Elohei Avraham avikha v-Elohei Yitzchaq*. The *nitzav alav* preposition is genuinely ambiguous between (a) 'above it' [the sulam] (ASV/LXX/Targum Onkelos/Rashi), (b) 'beside him' [Jacob] (NRSV/NJPS/Alter p. 149), and (c) 'above him.' WoH 'above it' is defensible — it preserves the sulam-top architecture that the v 17 *sha'ar ha-shamayim* assumes — and the dispute is documented. The two-generation ancestral-god self-disclosure formula (Gen 26:24 → 28:13 → Exod 3:6 culmination) per Alt 1929 is correctly identified. Land-promise lexeme via existing *zera-eretz-promise* entry.

Re-parsed MT: *v-hayah zarakha ka-afar ha-aretz... v-nivrakhu vekha kol-mishpechot ha-adamah u-v-zarekha*. The niphal *nivrakhu* MT-pointing is preserved (per project MT-fidelity policy) and rendered passive 'shall be blessed.' The doubled *vekha ... u-v-zarekha* unique-occurrence is correctly identified; seed-triad and niphal/hithpael entries appropriately extended. The aretz/adamah lexical distinction is preserved ('earth' / 'ground'). Defensible.

Re-parsed MT: *v-hineh anokhi imakh u-shmartikha b-khol asher telekh va-hashivotikha el-ha-adamah ha-zot ki lo e'ezovkha*. The Editor's call NOT to apply *al-tira* (the lexeme is absent here) and instead to extend *elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula* to v 15 is philologically correct. The compound presence/guarding/return/non-forsaking promise is the editorial-foundation of Ya'aqov's v 20-22 reciprocal vow. Faithful.

Re-parsed MT: *va-yiqatz Ya'aqov mi-shenato va-yomer akhen yesh YHWH ba-maqom ha-zeh v-anokhi lo yadati*. The *akhen yesh* + divine-name + *ba-maqom ha-zeh* + *v-anokhi lo yadati* construction is virtually unique in the HB. Cross-corpus structural cognates (Exod 3:5; Josh 5:15; Judg 13:22) correctly identified though they lack the *yesh* construction. ASV-baseline translation is faithful.

citations: Cross Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic (1973) ch. 1
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed MT: *va-yira va-yomar mah-norah ha-maqom ha-zeh ein zeh ki im-beit Elohim v-zeh sha'ar ha-shamayim*. The *beit Elohim* + *sha'ar ha-shamayim* compound is the chapter's keystone cultic-formula. The Akkadian *bab-ili* parallel is mainstream ANE-comparative scholarship (Heidel 1951 standard reference). The Gen 11:4 anti-intertext (Babel-failure / Ya'aqov-discovery) is HB-internal-explicit. The 'house of Elohim' + 'gate of the heavens' rendering preserves Elohim-transliteration and literal-plural *ha-shamayim*; reads as defensible scholarly translation. NT John 1:51 + Gen Rab 69:7 receptions flagged-not-preempted in apparatus, NOT in English text. The WoH lens-distinctive synthesis (sha'ar-shamayim-as-physical-gate) is reserved for the wiki — discipline held.

verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed MT: *va-yashkem Ya'aqov ba-boqer va-yiqach et-ha-even asher sam m'ra'ashotav va-yasem otah matzevah va-yitzoq shemen al-roshah*. The matzevah lexeme is grammatically explicit; the cross-corpus patriarchal-affirmation (Gen 28:18,22; 31:13,45,51-52; 35:14,20; Exod 24:4) vs Deuteronomic-prohibition (Lev 26:1; Deut 7:5; 12:3; 16:22; 2 Kgs 17:10; 18:4; 23:14) vs prophetic-lament (Hos 3:4; 10:1-2; Mic 5:13) distribution is documentary. Re-parsed MT: *va-yiqra et-shem ha-maqom ha-hu Beit-El v-ulam Luz shem-ha-ir la-rishonah*. The Beit-El / Luz name-doublet and cross-corpus distribution (Gen 35:6-7; Josh 16:2; 18:13; Judg 1:23-26) correctly identified. Transliteration consistent with chapter convention. Faithful.

The cognate-accusative *va-yidar... neder* is HB-first; cross-corpus vow-tradition (Num 21:2; 30; Judg 11:30-39; 1 Sam 1:11; 2 Sam 15:7-8; Eccl 5:3-5; Jonah 1:16) verifiable. Re-parsed MT: *v-shavti b-shalom el-beit avi v-hayah YHWH li le-Elohim*. The apodosis-opener with the *am-li / li-le-Elohim* covenantal-formula pre-figuring the Sinai-cluster (Exod 6:7; Lev 26:12; Jer 7:23; Ezek 36:28). ASV-baseline translation is faithful.

Re-parsed MT: *v-ha-even ha-zot asher samti matzevah yihyeh beit Elohim v-khol asher titen-li aser a'asrenu lakh*. The second cognate-accusative (*aser a'asrenu* — piel infinitive-absolute + piel imperfect 1cs) is the most-emphatic Hebrew tithe-formula; ASV 'I will surely give a tenth' preserves it. Second patriarchal tithe (after Avraham at Gen 14:20) cross-corpus correctly identified. The verse's binding of matzevah-as-beit-Elohim with the tithe-promise into a single cultic institution is mainstream modern-critical reading. Faithful.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק אֶֽל־יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹת֑וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֙הוּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq called Ya'aqov, and blessed him, and charged him, and said to him, You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Kena'an.

paragraphs.text: ק֥וּם לֵךְ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם בֵּ֥יתָה בְתוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ וְקַח־לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ׃

i18n.en: Arise, go to Paddan-Aram, to the house of Betu'el your mother's father, and take yourself a wife from there from the daughters of Lavan your mother's brother.

paragraphs.text: וְאֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְיַפְרְךָ֖ וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְהָיִ֖יתָ לִקְהַ֥ל עַמִּֽים׃

i18n.en: And El Shaddai bless you, and make you fruitful, and multiply you, that you may become an assembly of peoples.

paragraphs.commentary:
Yitzchaq's commissioning blessing pairs two distinctive lexemes. *El Shaddai* — the divine-name compound the project preserves in transliteration against the conventional *God Almighty* — opens the patriarchal-fertility-blessing in its canonical-P register (Gen 17:1; 28:3; 35:11; 43:14; 48:3; 49:25). See [el-shaddai](#el-shaddai) for the West-Semitic-mountain-god / Deir Alla *shdyn* etymology and the P-document Exod 6:3 source-critical claim.

The second distinctive lexeme is *q'hal amim* (קְהַל עַמִּים) — *assembly of peoples*. This is the patriarchal-blessing-formula's first use of *q'hal* (the cultic-assembly noun otherwise tied to Israelite legal-cultic gatherings: *q'hal YHWH* at Num 16:3; 20:4; Deut 23:2-9; *q'hal Elohim* at Neh 13:1). The *q'hal X* construct recurs only in this patriarchal-blessing cluster — Gen 28:3, Gen 35:11 (*q'hal goyim*, at Ya'aqov's Bethel-return), Gen 48:4 (Ya'aqov's blessing to Yosef) — and binds the three blessing-moments into a single editorial unit. Sarna *JPS* p. 196 and Westermann *Genesis 12-36* read the *q'hal* as cultic-register imported into the multiplication-promise: the patriarch's progeny will not merely be numerous but will constitute a worship-community. Translation renders *assembly of peoples* (NRSV-adjacent) — preserving the cultic register against the looser *company* (ASV/KJV) and *community* (NJPS).

paragraphs.text: וְיִֽתֶּן־לְךָ֙ אֶת־בִּרְכַּ֣ת אַבְרָהָ֔ם לְךָ֖ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֣ אִתָּ֑ךְ לְרִשְׁתְּךָ֙ אֶת־אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר־נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְאַבְרָהָֽם׃

i18n.en: And give you the blessing of Avraham, to you and to your seed with you, that you may possess the land of your sojournings, which Elohim gave to Avraham.

paragraphs.commentary: *Birkat Avraham* (בִּרְכַּת אַבְרָהָם) — *the blessing of Avraham* — is named here, for the first time in the patriarchal corpus, as a discrete bequeathable item. The blessing previously narrated as a sequence of YHWH-to-Avraham speech-acts (Gen 12:1-3; 15; 17; 22:17-18) is here reified into a single transferable property — a *berakhah* the patriarch can pass on. The lexicalization is editorially load-bearing: from Gen 28 forward the *birkat Avraham* functions as the patriarchal-line's signature inheritance, distinguishable from the material *yerushah* (land-possession) it underwrites. See [birkat-avraham-blessing-transmission](#birkat-avraham-blessing-transmission). Pauline reception at Gal 3:14 (*hē eulogia tou Abraam*) reads the Genesis lexicalization as the textual ground for the gospel-to-the-gentiles extension; flagged-not-preempted (Sarna p. 197; Westermann p. 449).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֑ם אֶל־לָבָ֤ן בֶּן־בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י אֲחִ֣י רִבְקָ֔ה אֵ֥ם יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְעֵשָֽׂו׃

i18n.en: And Yitzchaq sent Ya'aqov away, and he went to Paddan-Aram to Lavan son of Betu'el the Arammi, brother of Rivkah, the mother of Ya'aqov and Esav.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֗ו כִּֽי־בֵרַ֣ךְ יִצְחָק֮ אֶֽת־יַעֲקֹב֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם לָקַֽחַת־ל֥וֹ מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֑ה בְּבָרֲכ֣וֹ אֹת֔וֹ וַיְצַ֤ו עָלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא־תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן׃

i18n.en: And Esav saw that Yitzchaq had blessed Ya'aqov and sent him away to Paddan-Aram, to take himself a wife from there; and that as he blessed him he had charged him, saying, You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Kena'an;

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל־אָבִ֖יו וְאֶל־אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֥נָֽה אֲרָֽם׃

i18n.en: And that Ya'aqov obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Paddan-Aram;

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י רָע֖וֹת בְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן בְּעֵינֵ֖י יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִֽיו׃

i18n.en: and Esav saw that the daughters of Kena'an were evil in the eyes of Yitzchaq his father;

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶל־יִשְׁמָעֵ֑אל וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת־מָחֲלַ֣ת ׀ בַּת־יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן־אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת עַל־נָשָׁ֖יו ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: and Esav went to Yishma'el, and took Machalat the daughter of Yishma'el the son of Avraham, the sister of Nevayot, to be his wife, in addition to the wives he had.

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִבְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ חָרָֽנָה׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov went out from Be'er Sheva, and went toward Charan.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּפְגַּ֨ע בַּמָּק֜וֹם וַיָּ֤לֶן שָׁם֙ כִּי־בָ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וַיִּקַּח֙ מֵאַבְנֵ֣י הַמָּק֔וֹם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַהֽוּא׃

i18n.en: And he lighted upon the place, and lodged there, for the sun had set; and he took one of the stones of the place, and put it under his head, and lay down in that place to sleep.

paragraphs.commentary:
Two editorial signals in a single clause. *Va-yifga ba-maqom* — *he lighted upon / encountered the place* — uses the verb *paga* (פָּגַע), which ranges across the HB from neutral *meet / come upon* (Gen 32:2; Exod 5:20) to the intensive *fall upon, attack, intercede* (Josh 2:16; Isa 53:6, 12; Job 21:15). The chapter's verb is genuinely ambiguous between accidental-encounter (ASV *lighted upon*; Sarna, Westermann) and the rabbinic-tradition's *the place leapt out to meet him* (Gen Rab 68:9; Rashi). Translation preserves ASV's *lighted upon* — the chance-meeting register the v 16 *I did not know* discovery-formula assumes.

The second signal is the **definite article on *ha-maqom*** (the place, three times in the verse: *ba-maqom*, *ha-maqom*, *ba-maqom ha-hu*). The definite-articled *ha-maqom* is recognized in modern critical scholarship as a technical cultic-site designator across the patriarchal corpus (Gen 12:6; 22:3-4, 14; 28:11, 16-17, 19; 35:7, 14-15 — Sarna p. 198; Speiser p. 218). The article signals an already-recognized sacred-site: the chance encounter is with a place that was already a *maqom*, even if Ya'aqov does not know it yet (the v 16 *anokhi lo yadati* — *I did not know*). See [paga-ba-maqom-cultic-encounter](#paga-ba-maqom-cultic-encounter).

paragraphs.text: וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה סֻלָּם֙ מֻצָּ֣ב אַ֔רְצָה וְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ מַגִּ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה וְהִנֵּה֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים וְיֹרְדִ֖ים בּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And he dreamed, and behold, a stairway set up on the earth, and its top reached to the heavens; and behold, the messengers of Elohim ascending and descending on it.

paragraphs.commentary:
*Sulam* (סֻלָּם) — the chapter's keystone noun — is a true hapax. The word appears nowhere else in the Hebrew Bible. The two competing readings are old and still genuinely disputed.

**(a) Ladder.** LXX *klimax*, Vulgate *scala*, the traditional rendering preserved across ASV, KJV, NJPS, and NRSV. The reading assumes an unattested cognate to the Akkadian *simmiltu* via a metathesis or intermediate form. It is the rendering everyone recognizes.

**(b) Stairway / staircase / ramp.** The modern critical preference (Sarna *JPS* p. 198; Speiser *AB* p. 218; Hamilton *NICOT* pp. 240-241; Houtman, *VT* 27, 1977, 'What did Jacob see in his dream at Bethel?'). The argument: *sulam* is cognate with Akkadian *simmiltu* via a stable phonological correspondence; *simmiltu* in Mesopotamian literary and architectural texts denotes the **ziggurat staircase** — the great processional ramp on the stepped-temple-tower. The Nergal-and-Ereshkigal myth preserves *simmiltu ša šamê* — *the stairway of the heavens* — as a fixed cosmographic phrase. The chapter's *rosho magia ha-shamayma* (its top reaches the heavens) is a near-direct verbal echo of the Babel-builders' *u-rosho ba-shamayim* (Gen 11:4), and the v 17 *sha'ar ha-shamayim* (gate of the heavens) is the literal Akkadian *bab-ili* (Babel = *gate of god*). The chapter's wider Akkadian-architectural vocabulary makes the stairway-reading editorially load-bearing.

Translation: **stairway**, following the modern critical consensus. The ASV/LXX *ladder* is preserved in apparatus. See [sulam-stairway-or-ladder](#sulam-stairway-or-ladder).

The second figure of the verse is the **plural** *malakhei Elohim olim v-yordim bo* — *messengers of Elohim ascending and descending on it*. Note the word-order: **ascending before descending**, against the natural expectation that messengers *from the heavens* would descend first. The plural-messenger image is unique to this verse in the patriarchal narratives; the prior Gen 21:17 *mal'akh Elohim* and the Gen 16 / 22 *mal'akh YHWH* are all singular. Westermann reads the plural as the E-document's broader pattern of mediated divine-immanence (Gen 20:3 dream-mediation; Gen 31:11 the *mal'akh ha-Elohim* in Ya'aqov's dream; Gen 46:2 visions of the night). NT reception at John 1:51 (Jesus to Nathanael: *you shall see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man*) explicitly echoes this verse; rabbinic reception at Gen Rab 68:12 elaborates the ascending-descending order extensively. See [malakhei-elohim-ascending-descending](#malakhei-elohim-ascending-descending). The singular-construction governing entry [malakh-elohim-messenger](#malakh-elohim-messenger) is also referenced for the *mal'akh Elohim* lexeme family.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה נִצָּ֣ב עָלָיו֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יךָ וֵאלֹהֵ֖י יִצְחָ֑ק הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב עָלֶ֔יהָ לְךָ֥ אֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה וּלְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And behold, YHWH stood above it, and said, I am YHWH, the Elohim of Avraham your father, and the Elohim of Yitzchaq; the land on which you are lying, to you will I give it, and to your seed.

paragraphs.commentary:
Two editorially-distinct philological cruxes in a single verse.

**(i) *Nitzav alav* — the deity's position.** The preposition *alav* (עָלָיו) is genuinely ambiguous between three referents. **(a)** *Above it* — the *sulam* — the deity at the top of the stairway, consistent with the v 17 *sha'ar ha-shamayim* gate-of-heavens architecture (ASV *above it*; LXX; Targum Onkelos; Rashi). **(b)** *Beside him* — the deity standing beside the sleeping patriarch — supported by the common *al*-with-personal-referent sense of *beside, near* (NRSV; NJPS *stood beside him*; Alter 2004 p. 149 with extensive note); reinforced by the unambiguous *imakh* (with you) of v 15. **(c)** *Above him* — a third spatial reading. Translation: *stood above it* (ASV / LXX default) — preserving the *sulam*-top reading that the v 17 *sha'ar ha-shamayim* architecture assumes. The dispute is documented in apparatus. See [yhwh-nitzav-alav-ladder-position-dispute](#yhwh-nitzav-alav-ladder-position-dispute).

**(ii) The ancestral-god self-disclosure formula.** The deity's speech opens with *anokhi YHWH Elohei Avraham avikha v-Elohei Yitzchaq* — *I am YHWH, the Elohim of Avraham your father and the Elohim of Yitzchaq*. This is the **two-generation expansion** of the formula whose foundational deployment was at Gen 26:24 (to Yitzchaq: *anokhi Elohei Avraham avikha*) and which culminates in the canonical three-patriarchal compound at Exod 3:6 (*Elohei Avraham Elohei Yitzchaq v-Elohei Ya'aqov*). The pattern recurs across the patriarchal cycle at Gen 31:5, 31:42, 32:10, 35:1, 46:1, 46:3; the Alt 1929 *Der Gott der Väter* reconstruction reads it as evidence of pre-Mosaic ancestral-god clan-religion. See [anokhi-elohei-X-avikha-ancestral-god-formula](#anokhi-elohei-X-avikha-ancestral-god-formula). The verse's land-promise *l-kha etenenah u-l-zarekha* recurs through the Genesis land-promise cluster covered by [zera-eretz-promise](#zera-eretz-promise).

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֤ה זַרְעֲךָ֙ כַּעֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָרַצְתָּ֛ יָ֥מָּה וָקֵ֖דְמָה וְצָפֹ֣נָה וָנֶ֑גְבָּה וְנִבְרֲכ֥וּ בְךָ֛ כָּל־מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הָאֲדָמָ֖ה וּבְזַרְעֶֽךָ׃

i18n.en: And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth, and you shall spread abroad to the west, and to the east, and to the north, and to the south; and in you and in your seed shall all the families of the ground be blessed.

paragraphs.commentary: The verse re-applies to Ya'aqov two Abraham-cycle promise-figures. **(i)** *Ka-afar ha-aretz* — *as the dust of the earth* — the keystone of the patriarchal-seed-comparison-triad (dust / stars / sand on the seashore), foundationally deployed at Gen 13:16 and reapplied to Yitzchaq at Gen 26:4 (stars-form). See [patriarchal-seed-comparison-triad](#patriarchal-seed-comparison-triad). **(ii)** *V-nivrekhu vekha kol-mishpechot ha-adamah* — *in you all the families of the ground shall be blessed* — the universal-blessing-formula, MT-pointed *niphal* (passive) at this verse, matching Gen 12:3 and 18:18 and contrasting with the *hithpael* pointings at Gen 22:18 and 26:4. Translation follows the MT-fidelity policy and renders *shall be blessed* (passive). The doubled *vekha ... u-v-zarekha* (in you ... and in your seed) is unique to this verse — the only patriarchal occurrence of the doubled-prepositional construction with both subjects. See [nivrakhu-bekha-niphal-hithpael](#nivrakhu-bekha-niphal-hithpael).

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י עִמָּ֗ךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּ֙יךָ֙ בְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר־תֵּלֵ֔ךְ וַהֲשִׁ֣בֹתִ֔יךָ אֶל־הָאֲדָמָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את כִּ֚י לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱזָבְךָ֔ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם־עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר־דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And behold, I am with you, and will keep you wherever you go, and will bring you back to this ground; for I will not leave you until I have done that which I have spoken to you of.

paragraphs.commentary: The verse is one of the corpus's foundational divine-presence-and-protection promises, but it does **not** contain the *al-tira* (fear-not) particle of Gen 21:17 / 26:24. The deity opens with *hineh anokhi imakh* — *behold, I am with you* — the divine-self-disclosure variant of the divine-presence-formula covered by [elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula](#elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula) (foundational external-recognition deployment at Gen 21:22 with Avimelekh; divine self-disclosure deployment at Gen 26:3, 26:24, 28:15, 31:3, 46:4). Three additional clauses extend the promise: *u-shmartikha* (I will guard you), *va-hashivotikha* (I will bring you back), and the closing *ki lo e'ezovkha* (for I will not forsake you). The compound — *anokhi imakh* + guarding + return + non-forsaking — recurs across the Ya'aqov-cycle (Gen 31:3, 35:3, 46:4) and supplies the verbal content of Ya'aqov's reciprocal vow at vv 20-22.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּיקַ֣ץ יַעֲקֹב֮ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָכֵן֙ יֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֥א יָדָֽעְתִּי׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov awoke from his sleep, and said, Surely YHWH is in this place, and I did not know it.

paragraphs.commentary: *Akhen yesh YHWH ba-maqom ha-zeh v-anokhi lo yadati* — *Surely YHWH is in this place, and I did not know it*. The construction is virtually unique to this verse in the HB: *akhen* (truly, surely) + *yesh* (existence-particle) + divine-name + *ba-maqom ha-zeh* + the *v-anokhi lo yadati* (I-did-not-know) confession. The verse stands as the HB's foundational *I-did-not-know-this-place-was-sacred* moment. Structural cognates: Exod 3:5 (Moses at the burning bush — *the place where you stand is holy ground*, without the *yesh* construction); Josh 5:15 (parallel formula); Judg 13:22 (Manoah's response after the *mal'akh YHWH* departs). The verse pairs with the v 17 *mah-norah ha-maqom ha-zeh* awe-formula as the two halves of the patriarchal discovery-of-the-sacred. The v 11 definite-articled *ha-maqom* now closes the circle: the place was always a *maqom*; the discovery is that Ya'aqov *did not know*. See [akhen-yesh-yhwh-discovery-of-sacred-place](#akhen-yesh-yhwh-discovery-of-sacred-place).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּירָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מַה־נּוֹרָ֖א הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה אֵ֣ין זֶ֗ה כִּ֚י אִם־בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְזֶ֖ה שַׁ֥עַר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם׃

i18n.en: And he was afraid, and said, How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of Elohim, and this is the gate of the heavens.

paragraphs.commentary:
The chapter's keystone cultic-formula. Two compound lexemes are paired in a single declaration.

**(i) *Beit Elohim*** — *house of Elohim*. The foundational HB temple-cultic-site formula. The construct binds *bayit* (house, dwelling) to *Elohim*, naming the place as the deity's dwelling-house. The lexeme will recur across the HB for both Bethel and the Jerusalem temple (with *beit Elohim* and *beit YHWH* in free variation across Chronicles, Ezra, Nehemiah). The v 19 etymology — *va-yiqra et-shem ha-maqom ha-hu Beit-El* — explicitly grounds the place-name in this verse's *beit Elohim* declaration: the place is named for what Ya'aqov said it was.

**(ii) *Sha'ar ha-shamayim*** — *gate of the heavens*. The chapter's most editorially-distinctive lexeme. The compound is functionally identical to the Akkadian **bab-ili** (gate of god), from which the city-name Babylon derives, and which Gen 11 polemically reads as *Babel* (from the root *b-l-l*, *confuse*). The Gen 28:17 *sha'ar ha-shamayim* is the chapter's verbal echo of and counterpoint to the Babel-builders' attempted *u-rosho ba-shamayim* (Gen 11:4): where the Babel-builders tried to build the gate-to-heaven and were scattered, Ya'aqov **discovers** the gate-to-heaven and is blessed. Heidel *The Babylonian Genesis* (1951) and the standard ANE-comparative literature on the *bab-ili* / *simmiltu ša šamê* cluster (cf. ANET) document the Akkadian background.

Downstream receptions are extensive and flagged-not-preempted: NT John 1:51 (Jesus as the *sha'ar* / gateway in the Son-of-Man Christology); rabbinic Gen Rab 69:7 (the *maqom* identified with the future Temple Mount). Modern critical readings (Westermann pp. 454-455; Sarna pp. 198-199; Cross *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* 1973 ch. 1 on the El-Bethel cult-site; Albright *Yahweh and the Gods of Canaan* 1968) read the verse as the Bethel-cult's foundation-narrative. The English renders *house of Elohim* and *gate of the heavens* — preserving the *Elohim* in transliteration and the literal-plural *ha-shamayim*. See [beit-elohim-shaar-ha-shamayim-cultic-formula](#beit-elohim-shaar-ha-shamayim-cultic-formula).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֜ב בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת־הָאֶ֙בֶן֙ אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֹתָ֖הּ מַצֵּבָ֑ה וַיִּצֹ֥ק שֶׁ֖מֶן עַל־רֹאשָֽׁהּ׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov rose up early in the morning, and took the stone that he had put under his head, and set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on the top of it.

paragraphs.commentary:
The HB's foundational patriarchal-*matzevah* (מַצֵּבָה) — the sacred standing-stone — and its first occurrence in Genesis. Ya'aqov takes the stone he had placed under his head, *sets it up as a matzevah*, and pours oil on its top. The act has a complex cross-corpus reception.

**Affirmatively present in the patriarchal cult.** Gen 28:18, 22; Gen 31:13 (the *mal'akh* explicitly identifies *the matzevah you anointed* — the back-reference confirms the editorial-status of the Bethel-matzevah); Gen 31:45, 51-52; Gen 35:14, 20 (Rachel's burial matzevah at Bethlehem); Exod 24:4 (Mosheh sets up twelve matzevot at Sinai).

**Explicitly outlawed in later Yahwism.** Lev 26:1 (*u-matzevah lo taqimu lakhem*); Deut 7:5; 12:3; 16:22 (*v-lo taqim l'kha matzevah asher sane YHWH Elohekha* — *you shall not raise up a matzevah, which YHWH your Elohim hates*); 2 Kgs 17:10; 18:4; 23:14 (Josiah's reform's matzevah-smashing).

**Lamented in the prophets.** Hos 3:4 (*ein matzevah*); Hos 10:1-2; Mic 5:13.

The patriarchal-affirmation / Deuteronomic-prohibition tension is one of the HB's most editorially-load-bearing cultic-history doublets: the patriarchs build the very cultic objects the later legislation prohibits. Alt 1929 *Der Gott der Väter*, Cross 1973 *Canaanite Myth and Hebrew Epic* ch. 1, Smith 2001 *The Origins of Biblical Monotheism*, and Mettinger 1995 *No Graven Image?* read the patriarchal-matzevah as evidence of the pre-Yahwistic patriarchal-El religion subsequently suppressed by Deuteronomic reform. Translation: *pillar* (ASV/KJV/NRSV/NJPS), with the matzevah-as-cultic-object register preserved in apparatus. See [matzevah-sacred-pillar-patriarchal-religion](#matzevah-sacred-pillar-patriarchal-religion). The oil-pouring (*va-yitzoq shemen al-roshah*) is the chapter's first HB anointing-of-a-cultic-object; the verb *yatzaq + shemen* recurs for the priestly-anointing legislation (Exod 29:7; Lev 8:12).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת־שֵֽׁם־הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בֵּֽית־אֵ֑ל וְאוּלָ֛ם ל֥וּז שֵׁם־הָעִ֖יר לָרִאשֹׁנָֽה׃

i18n.en: And he called the name of that place Beit-El; but the name of the city was Luz at the first.

paragraphs.commentary: *Beit-El* — *house of El* — is named here for the first time as a *patriarchal* renaming. The v 17 *beit Elohim* declaration is now lexicalized into the place-name. The earlier name *Luz* (לוּז, *almond / almond-tree* in post-biblical Hebrew, presumably the Canaanite-period name) is preserved as a doublet. The Luz / Beit-El name-doublet recurs across the HB: Gen 35:6-7 (Ya'aqov returns and renames the place *El Beit-El*); Josh 16:2; 18:13 (the Luz/Beit-El identification as a tribal-allotment boundary-marker); Judg 1:23-26 (the Beit-El capture-narrative with the Luz-people resettled elsewhere). The chapter's *Beit-El* will become the dynastic-cultic center of the northern kingdom under Yarov'am (1 Kgs 12:29-33) and the focus of the prophetic-critique cluster (Amos 7:13). See [bethel-luz-name-etymology](#bethel-luz-name-etymology).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּדַּ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב נֶ֣דֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם־יִהְיֶ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים עִמָּדִ֗י וּשְׁמָרַ֙נִי֙ בַּדֶּ֤רֶךְ הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ וְנָֽתַן־לִ֥י לֶ֛חֶם לֶאֱכֹ֖ל וּבֶ֥גֶד לִלְבֹּֽשׁ׃

i18n.en: And Ya'aqov vowed a vow, saying, If Elohim will be with me, and will keep me on this way that I am going, and will give me bread to eat and clothing to put on,

paragraphs.commentary: *Va-yidar Ya'aqov neder* — *Ya'aqov vowed a vow* — the **first explicit *neder* (vow) in the HB**. The cognate-accusative construction (*va-yidar... neder*) becomes the standard HB vow-formula and recurs at Num 21:2 (Israel's *cherem* vow before Arad); Num 30 (the vow-legislation); Judg 11:30-39 (Yiftach's failed vow); 1 Sam 1:11 (Channah's vow); 2 Sam 15:7-8 (Avshalom); Eccl 5:3-5 (the vow-discipline wisdom). The Ya'aqov-vow's content is **conditional and tripartite**: the protasis (vv 20-21a) names three divine actions — presence (*Elohim imadi*), guarding (*u-shmarani ba-derekh*), and provision-and-safe-return; the apodosis (vv 21b-22) names three reciprocal obligations — YHWH will be Ya'aqov's Elohim, the matzevah will be a *beit Elohim*, and Ya'aqov will tithe. The vow is thus structurally a covenant-of-reciprocity initiated from the human side, balancing the divine-initiated covenant of vv 13-15. ASV's *vowed a vow* preserves the cognate-accusative against the NRSV/NJPS smoothing *made a vow*. See [yaakov-vow-tithe-promise](#yaakov-vow-tithe-promise).

paragraphs.text: וְשַׁבְתִּ֥י בְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל־בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י לֵאלֹהִֽים׃

i18n.en: so that I come back to my father's house in peace, then YHWH shall be my Elohim;

paragraphs.commentary: The apodosis-opener of Ya'aqov's vow. *V-hayah YHWH li le-Elohim* — *YHWH shall be my Elohim* — restates the covenantal-formula known later as the *brit*-formula (the *am-li / li-le-Elohim* pair of Exod 6:7; Lev 26:12; Jer 7:23; Ezek 36:28). The verse marks the first patriarchal use of the formula. See [yaakov-vow-tithe-promise](#yaakov-vow-tithe-promise).

paragraphs.text: וְהָאֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּ֗את אֲשֶׁר־שַׂ֙מְתִּי֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתֶּן־לִ֔י עַשֵּׂ֖ר אֲעַשְּׂרֶ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ׃

i18n.en: and this stone, which I have set up as a pillar, shall be the house of Elohim; and of all that you give me I will surely give a tenth to you.

paragraphs.commentary: The vow's closing two reciprocal obligations bind together the chapter's two cultic institutions. **(i)** *V-ha-even ha-zot... yihyeh beit Elohim* — *and this stone... shall be the house of Elohim* — explicitly identifies the v 18 *matzevah* with the v 17 *beit Elohim*: the standing-stone is the proto-temple, the cultic anchor that will name the place. **(ii)** *Aser a-asrenu lakh* — the cognate-accusative *tithe-I-will-tithe* construction — the HB's **second pre-Sinai tithe** after Avraham's at Gen 14:20. The piel infinitive-absolute + piel imperfect 1cs is the most-emphatic Hebrew tithe-formula, equivalent to *I shall surely tithe*. The Avraham-tithe (Gen 14:20, to the El-Elyon priest Malki-Tzedek) and the Ya'aqov-tithe (Gen 28:22, to YHWH at Bethel) together establish the pre-Sinai patriarchal-tithe institution; both are flagged in [maaser-first-pre-sinai](#maaser-first-pre-sinai). Cross-corpus development: Lev 27:30-33 (the holiness-code tithe-law); Num 18:21-32 (the Levitical tithe); Deut 12:6, 14:22-29 (the Deuteronomic tithe-laws); Mal 3:8-10 (the post-exilic tithe-restoration). The verse is editorially distinctive in tying the tithe directly to the *matzevah* — stone and tithe form a single inaugural cultic institution. See [yaakov-vow-tithe-promise](#yaakov-vow-tithe-promise) and [matzevah-sacred-pillar-patriarchal-religion](#matzevah-sacred-pillar-patriarchal-religion).
